finding.title: NASA TechLeap Orbital Clarity Challenge opened with a $2 million award pool and up to $500,000 per winner across three phases
finding.source_name: NASA / Orbital Clarity Challenge official host
finding.observed: nasa techleap orbital clarity challenge | official nasa page published aug 19 2026 | challenge open aug 19 2026 | phase 1 registration closes oct 28 2026 | phase 1 submission closes nov 11 2026 | up to four winners may receive up to 500000 usd each across three phases | total award pool 2000000 usd | winning teams intended no-cost test flight
verified_facts: NASA states the challenge opened August 19, 2026.
Phase 1 registration closes October 28, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET.
Phase 1 submissions close November 11, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET.
The official host states an award pool of $2 million: up to four winners may receive up to $500,000 each across three phases.
Phase 1 winners receive $200,000 each; Phase 2 teams may receive an additional $200,000 each; Phase 3 teams may receive an additional $100,000 each.
NASA intends to offer each Phase 3 winner an orbital flight test at no cost.
Individuals must be U.S. citizens or U.S. permanent residents and at least 18 years old.
Organizations must be incorporated in and maintain a primary place of business in the United States.
Teams must consist of otherwise eligible individuals or organizations and be led by a U.S. citizen or permanent resident who is at least 18 years old.
Each eligible lead applicant may submit once, though a lead applicant may partner on another distinct submission.
Applicants may not receive U.S. government funding twice for the same scope of work; prior or current government-funded development can affect eligibility.
The challenge requires at least $250,000 in liability-insurance coverage or equivalent financial responsibility, with coverage conditions specified by the official host.
Standalone free-flying satellites are not eligible; proposed solutions must be compatible with hosted-payload integration on a commercial spacecraft.

Phase 1 submissions are scored by expert judges on a 1-5 rubric, normalized, and the top submissions proceed to a selection committee that chooses up to four winners using scores plus programmatic considerations.
